title: District 7 Ho Chi Minh City: Phu My Hung rental guide
description: District 7 (Phu My Hung), Ho Chi Minh City, for renters: its four new wards, the trip to the centre, asking rents dated 26 November 2026, and what to check.
h1: District 7, Ho Chi Minh City: a rental guide to Phu My Hung and the rest of the district
intro: District 7 is in the south of Ho Chi Minh City and contains the planned Phu My Hung area. Since 1 July 2025 it has officially been four wards: Tan Hung, Tan My, Tan Thuan and Phu Thuan. On 26 November 2026, the eno.vn HCMC Rent Index counted 111 District 7 homes listed for rent on eno.vn. According to Vietcetera, Phu My Hung is about 6.5 km south of the city centre.
keyPoints: **District 7 is no longer an official district.** Under Resolution 1685/NQ-UBTVQH15 of 16 June 2025, its ten wards became Tan Hung, Tan My, Tan Thuan and Phu Thuan. The new ward governments started work on 1 July 2025. Listings still say District 7.
**Phu My Hung is only part of District 7.** According to Savills (September 2026), it is a 750-hectare planned area in Tan My and Tan Hung wards, developed by Phu My Hung Development Corporation.

On 26 November 2026, the eno.vn [HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) gave these District 7 median asking rents: {{vnd:5400000}} a month for a studio, {{vnd:15000000}} for a one-bedroom and {{vnd:16800000}} for a two-bedroom.
On 26 November 2026, the HCMC Rent Index put the median asking rent for a District 7 one-bedroom only {{vnd:1800000}} below a two-bedroom's, so compare the two before you choose.
According to Vietcetera, Phu My Hung is about 6.5 km south of the city centre, or roughly 20 minutes away. Traffic decides how long the trip really takes.

sections.title: What is District 7 in Ho Chi Minh City like for renters?

blocks.text: District 7 is in the south of Ho Chi Minh City and has two kinds of area. One is the planned Phu My Hung area, with wide roads, high-rise apartments, a mall, a lake and international schools. The rest is ordinary city wards along Huynh Tan Phat and Nguyen Van Linh streets. Renters mostly choose District 7 for space, greenery and schools, not for being close to central nightlife.

According to Wikipedia, the former district covered about 36 km² and had 456,789 residents in 2024. District 4 lies to its north across the Te Channel, and Thu Duc lies across the Saigon River. District 8 and Binh Chanh are to the west and Nha Be is to the south. The Phu My Bridge has linked District 7 to Thu Duc since September 2009.
Is District 7 still a district?

District 7 stopped being an official district on 1 July 2025, when Vietnam abolished the district level. Under [Resolution 1685/NQ-UBTVQH15](https://english.luatvietnam.vn/co-cau-to-chuc/resolution-1685-nq-ubtvqh15-2025-reorganization-of-commune-level-administrative-divisions-of-ho-chi-minh-in-2025-403012-d1.html) of 16 June 2025, its ten wards were merged into four. The same resolution gives Ho Chi Minh City 168 units: 113 wards, 54 communes and 1 special zone. People, landlords and eno.vn listings still say 'District 7', and so does this guide. A lease or utility bill, however, will show the new ward name.
What is in Phu My Hung for daily life?

Wikipedia's page on the Phu My Hung urban area lists Crescent Lake and Crescent Mall, FV Hospital, Tam Duc Heart Hospital and Saigon South International School. It also lists the RMIT Vietnam campus, Fulbright University Vietnam and the Saigon Exhibition and Convention Center (SECC). According to the same page, the developer reported more than 30,000 residents in 2018, and more than half of them were foreigners, mainly from Korea, Japan, Taiwan and China. Vietcetera says locals call the area 'Little Seoul'. For school fees, see [international schools in Ho Chi Minh City](/guides/international-schools-in-ho-chi-minh-city).

sections.title: Phu My Hung compared with the rest of District 7

blocks.text: Phu My Hung is the planned, higher-end part of District 7. The other wards have a wider mix of homes, including small studios and duplex rooms, outside the planned grid. If a listing says 'District 7', find out which ward the home is in before you compare its price with another listing.

Phu My Hung is built and run by Phu My Hung Development Corporation, which has its centre in Tan My ward. According to Wikipedia, the company was founded in 1993 as a joint venture between Taiwan's CT&D Group and the Ho Chi Minh City government. Savills wrote in September 2026 that Phu My Hung covers 750 hectares, in five urban clusters in Tan My and Tan Hung wards. Wikipedia adds that the development reaches into the former District 8 and Binh Chanh, so not every 'Phu My Hung' address is in District 7.

blocks.title: Search both names
blocks.text: Many landlords still use the old ward names, such as Tan Phong or Tan Phu, so search for both the old and the new name. According to Wikipedia, most of Phu My Hung New City lies in the former Tan Phu and Tan Phong wards. Those wards are now part of Tan My and Tan Hung.

sections.title: How far is District 7 from central Ho Chi Minh City?

blocks.text: Vietcetera's guide to the city after the 2025 merger puts Phu My Hung about 6.5 km south of the city centre, or roughly 20 minutes away. The real journey time depends on the hour and on which bridge you cross, so time the trip at the hours you would really travel.

VinWonders' District 7 guide, published in December 2025, gives the distance from Tan Son Nhat Airport as about 13 to 17 km, depending on the route. By car or motorbike, its suggested route crosses the Khanh Hoi Bridge and the Tan Thuan 2 Bridge, then follows Nguyen Van Linh to Huynh Tan Phat. By bus, it suggests route 109 and then a change to route 72, 34, 38 or 140. VinWonders notes that this information may change.
Does District 7 suit a job in District 1?

District 7 suits a job in District 1 if your commute runs against the main traffic flow or you work split shifts. It suits you less if you have to cross the bridges at rush hour every day. Before you sign a lease, make the trip yourself, by Grab or by motorbike, at your real start and finish times. For your options, see [getting around Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/getting-around-ho-chi-minh-city) and [renting a motorbike in Ho Chi Minh City](/guides/renting-a-motorbike-in-ho-chi-minh-city).

sections.title: How much does it cost to rent in District 7?

blocks.text: A studio is the cheapest home in District 7, and anything from a one-bedroom up costs far more. On 26 November 2026, the eno.vn [HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) counted 111 District 7 homes listed on eno.vn, made up of 104 apartments and 7 houses. The index gives median asking prices, not signed rents, and landlords often accept less. It publishes a median only where there are at least 10 listings, so on 26 November 2026 it gave none for District 7 houses.

blocks.caption: District 7 (Phu My Hung): median asking rent for apartments by type, from the eno.vn HCMC Rent Index snapshot of 26 November 2026

blocks.text: On 26 November 2026, the HCMC Rent Index showed a big jump in median asking rent from a studio to a one-bedroom in District 7. The step from a one-bedroom up to a two-bedroom was only {{vnd:1800000}}. If you need a separate bedroom, then, look at two-bedroom flats as well.
How do I browse District 7 rentals by area and price?

To browse by area and price, open [District 7 rentals on eno.vn](/c/rentals/d7). You can filter by 1, 2 or 3 or more bedrooms and sort by price from low to high. A map view lets you keep to the wards you want. To compare District 7 with other districts, use the [HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index) or the [rent prices by district guide](/guides/rent-prices), and compare the same type of home. To look at nearby areas, start from [all Ho Chi Minh City rentals](/c/rentals).

sections.title: Questions to ask before you commit to District 7

blocks.text: Before you commit to District 7, confirm three things: the exact ward, the commute at your real hours, and what the rent includes. All three vary a lot within District 7. For the general rules on leases, bills and deposits, see [renting an apartment in Vietnam as a foreigner](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner) and the [rental deposit guide](/rental-deposit-vietnam).

items: **Which ward is the home in, by old and new name?** A home in Tan Thuan and a home in Tan My can both be advertised as 'District 7'.
**How long is the commute at 7am and at 6pm?** Check it on a map app at those times, not at midday.
**Is the home furnished, and what is extra?** Ask whether the management fee, parking, electricity and water are included, and how electricity is charged.
**Will the landlord make the residence declaration?** This is part of the tenancy. The [renting guide](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner) explains it.
**How much is the deposit, and when is it returned?** Get the answer written into the lease, not only in a chat message.
**Is this the asking price?** Listed rents are asking prices, and landlords often accept less.

blocks.text: If you are moving with children, weigh Phu My Hung's schools against your commute. For more on that choice, see [moving to Vietnam with a family](/teach-in-vietnam/moving-to-vietnam-with-family-as-a-teacher) and [where to live in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/where-to-live-in-ho-chi-minh-city-as-a-teacher).

sections.title: How do I find out if a District 7 home is still free before I travel?

blocks.text: To find out whether a District 7 home is still free, message the landlord, agent or partner who listed it in eno.vn chat. On listings from GoPlus, an official eno.vn partner, GoPlus answers its own listings there. On a linked listing, the button opens the original posting on its source site, where you contact the advertiser.

items.title: Shortlist by ward and type
items.text: Open [District 7 rentals](/c/rentals/d7), filter by bedrooms and sort by price. Shortlist a few homes and note the ward of each one.

items.title: Message the landlord or agent
items.text: Ask in eno.vn chat whether each home on your shortlist is still free. On [GoPlus](/goplus) listings, GoPlus answers in eno.vn chat. On a linked listing, the button opens the original posting on its source site.

items.title: Ask what the price includes
items.text: In the same conversation, ask about furniture, the management fee, parking, how electricity is charged and the deposit.

items.title: Ask again before you fly
items.text: Ask again a few days before you travel. A home that was free weeks earlier may have been rented out since.

items.title: View the home before you pay
items.text: Book viewings for your first days in the city, and read the lease before you pay any deposit.

blocks.text: Do not send a deposit for a District 7 home that you have not seen, or that someone you trust has not viewed for you. Before you pay, read the [safety page](/safety) and the [deposit guide](/rental-deposit-vietnam).

sections.title: A short decision checklist for District 7

blocks.text: District 7 is the right choice if most of the points below are true for you. If your work, school or social life is mostly north of the Saigon River, look at other districts first.

items: Your work or your children's school is in or near District 7, or you commute against the rush-hour traffic.
Your budget fits the median asking rent for the type of home you need (see the 26 November 2026 table above).
You know the ward of every home on your shortlist, by both its old and its new name.
You have timed the commute at your real hours.
You have asked what the rent includes and how the deposit is returned.
You have asked the landlord or agent again, a few days before you travel, whether the home is still free.
You have budgeted for the move itself. See [moving apartment in Saigon](/guides/saigonmoving) and [furnishing a home](/furnishing-a-home-in-vietnam).

sections.title: What this guide does not cover

items: A comparison of every Ho Chi Minh City neighbourhood. For that, see [where to live in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/where-to-live-in-ho-chi-minh-city-as-a-teacher) and [rent prices by district](/guides/rent-prices).
Leases, bills and the landlord's paperwork in detail. These are covered in [renting an apartment in Vietnam as a foreigner](/renting-an-apartment-vietnam-foreigner).
Renting out your own District 7 flat. For that, see [renting your apartment to foreigners](/guides/rent-your-apartment-to-foreigners-ho-chi-minh-city).
Signed rents in District 7. None of the sources used here publishes them. The figures here are asking prices.

faqs.q: Where is District 7 in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: District 7 is in the south of Ho Chi Minh City. According to Wikipedia, District 4 lies to its north across the Te Channel and Thu Duc across the Saigon River. District 8 and Binh Chanh are to the west and Nha Be is to the south. District 7 stopped being an official district on 1 July 2025, when its wards became Tan Hung, Tan My, Tan Thuan and Phu Thuan, but listings still use the name.

faqs.q: What does HCM mean in a District 7 address?
faqs.a: HCM is a common short form of Ho Chi Minh City. The city is also written HCMC or TP.HCM and is still widely called Saigon, so an address ending 'District 7, HCM' is in Ho Chi Minh City. Since 1 July 2025, official addresses give the ward instead of the district. A District 7 lease or bill may therefore show Tan Hung, Tan My, Tan Thuan or Phu Thuan ward.

faqs.q: Is District 7 the same as Phu My Hung?
faqs.a: District 7 and Phu My Hung are not the same place. Phu My Hung is a planned urban area developed by Phu My Hung Development Corporation, a joint venture founded in 1993. According to Savills (September 2026), it covers 750 hectares in Tan My and Tan Hung wards. Tan Thuan and Phu Thuan wards, also part of the former District 7, lie outside Phu My Hung.

faqs.q: How far is District 7 from District 1 in Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: According to Vietcetera's guide to Ho Chi Minh City after the 2025 merger, the Phu My Hung area of District 7 is about 6.5 km south of the city centre, or roughly 20 minutes away. Journey times in Ho Chi Minh City depend heavily on traffic and the time of day. Check the route on a live map app at your real commuting times before you sign a District 7 lease.

faqs.q: How much is rent in District 7 Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Rent in District 7 depends mainly on the type of home. On 26 November 2026, the eno.vn HCMC Rent Index counted 111 District 7 homes listed on eno.vn. Studios had much lower median asking rents than one-bedroom flats, and the gap between a one-bedroom and a two-bedroom was small. The figures for each type are in this guide's rent table. They are asking prices, not signed rents.

faqs.q: What is District 7 called now after the 2025 changes?
faqs.a: The former District 7 is now four wards of Ho Chi Minh City: Tan Hung, Tan My, Tan Thuan and Phu Thuan. Resolution 1685/NQ-UBTVQH15 of 16 June 2025 merged its ten old wards into these four. The new ward governments began work on 1 July 2025, when Vietnam abolished the district level. Landlords, drivers and rental listings still use the name District 7.

faqs.q: How do I check a District 7 rental is still available before I travel?
faqs.a: To check that a District 7 rental on eno.vn is still available, message the landlord, agent or partner who listed it in eno.vn chat. GoPlus, an official eno.vn partner, answers its own listings there. On a linked listing, the button opens the original posting on its source site, where you contact the advertiser. Ask again a few days before you travel, because District 7 homes can be rented out quickly.
